notices.capped.title: There is not enough room for Hifth to work offline
notices.capped.body: The browser gives this site only a small amount of space, so saved pages may be deleted. Check the free space on your device, and the «clear site data when all windows are closed» setting under privacy.
notices.install-ios.title: Install Hifth so it stays with you offline
notices.install-ios.body: From the browser's share button, choose «Add to Home Screen». Without installing, Safari deletes saved pages after seven days without opening the app.
notices.install-prompt.title: Install Hifth so it works offline
notices.install-prompt.body: Installing keeps the pages you have visited saved on your device.
aboutLede: Hifth is a navigation instrument for the mus'haf: pick an ayah and it takes you to its mutashabihat. No account, no server, no tracking — the pages and the data are loaded onto your device.
aboutCaveat: The printed mus'haf is the reference. What Hifth shows is an aid to revision, not a substitute for it.

verseGesturesTitle: Tap and hold on a verse
verseGesturesNote: What your finger does on a verse. Tap hides the bars: a tap hides or shows the bars, and a hold opens the verse's menu. Tap opens the full menu: a tap or a hold opens it, and full screen is a button below the page. Hold opens a small menu: a tap opens the menu as before, and a hold opens a small menu beside the verse. With a mouse a click always opens the menu, and F switches full screen.
jumpArrowsNote: Where your memory leaves a verse. Stay on the page: a faint wavy line under the word, with the verses you went to, so you see it before you reach it. Only when you ask: the page stays clean, and a verse's arrow shows while its list is open, or every arrow while the Jump tool is on. The red mark by the verse number shows either way.
cardEdgeClear: Card stops short of the edge
cardEdgeTurns: Grab the edge through the card
cardEdgeNote: On a two-page spread, a note or a list lies over the facing page. Arrows and keys: the card covers the page's outer edge, so the arrows and the keys turn the page while it is open. Card stops short of the edge: the card leaves the outer edge uncovered, so you can grab it and turn the page as usual. Grab the edge through the card: the card covers the edge, and a drag from the edge closes the card and turns the page.
openingTextNote: The book's first two pages hold less text than the rest. Large text: their text fills the width of the page. Usual size: their text keeps the size of every other page, in the middle of the page.
longVerseTitle: A verse a little too tall for the room above a note
longVerseNote: On a screen held upright, a verse can come out a few lines taller than the room the note leaves above it. Page a little smaller: the page is drawn a little smaller so the whole verse shows, and the note keeps its height. Note a little shorter: the note opens a little shorter, and the page stays at the size the link opened it.
lookalikeCompareTitle: Look-alikes that share words in more than one place
lookalikeCompareNote: Some look-alike verses share a run of words that comes more than once, so no one place can be marked as the match. Mark every shared stretch: opening the row washes every run of two words or more the two share, and what lies between them. Side by side, unmarked: the two verses are shown as printed, with nothing marked. Pairs that share one stretch keep their single mark either way.
passageRowsTitle: A passage listed beside a verse inside it
passageRowsNote: Some look-alikes are listed twice: once as a whole passage, and again as a single verse inside it. Show both rows: each stays where it falls in the list. Verse under its passage: the verse sits set in, right under the passage. Verse only: the passage row is left out, and the verse keeps its own row.
ribbonLengthTitle: How far a bookmark's ribbon hangs
ribbonLengthNote: Short: the ribbon stops above the first line, so the first words of the page stay in view; open it to see its name. Long: it hangs down over the first lines, with its name written along it.
lookalikePreviewTitle: The words a look-alike shares, before it is opened
lookalikePreviewNote: Under each look-alike in a list, the words it shares with your verse. Cut from the page: the shared words as the mus'haf prints them. As a count: how many words it shares. Not shown: open a row to see them.
relatedListNote: A note can point to more verses than fit in a short list. The first eight: the list shows eight, and a line under them says how many more there are and shows them. All at once: the list shows every related verse from the start.
scopeLookTitle: Picking what a note is about
scopeLookNote: How a note shows the parts it can be about, from one harakah to the whole Qur'an. Sideways: short lines in a row, the whole Qur'an the longest. Lines: the same lines stacked, the narrowest on top. Pointing at a line shows its letter. Pyramid: every part named. Slim: a thin pyramid of letters. Steps: bars rising from harakah to the whole Qur'an. One line: the letters in a row. In every one, a part's letter picks it.

penGrip: Move the tools: drag to any edge
penHomeNote: On a computer, or an iPad held sideways. Above the page: a row of tools over the book, as before. Floating: drag it by its handle to any edge of the window. Mark up button: the tools wait behind one button in the bottom row, and the page is for reading until you open them. Down the side: the tools stand in the empty margin beside the book, and go to the bottom row where there is no margin.
railHomeTitle: Where the look-alike buttons go when the page fills the screen
railHomeNote: On a computer or an iPad. The buttons for similar verses stand beside the page; when the page is magnified to fill the screen there is no room beside it, so they leave the page. Bottom row: beside the trail of verses you came from. Tool row: at the end of the row of tools above the page, or in the bottom row when the tools are somewhere else.
